title: Takrur
capsule: Takrur was a Senegambian kingdom centered on the middle Senegal River—one of the earliest sub-Saharan polities to adopt Islam, when ruler War Jabi converted and imposed Sharia around 1035 CE, making it a landmark in West African Islamic history. At its apex in the eleventh century it rivaled the Ghana Empire as a regional power, and its cavalry reportedly fought in the Almoravid victory at the Battle of Sagrajas (1086). After the fall of its Manna ruling dynasty, the Mali Empire absorbed Takrur around 1286; the Jolof Empire subsequently held the region before the Fula Denanke dynasty supplanted it from 1559.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Takrur's territorial extent is poorly documented; the kingdom is attested primarily through Arab geographical sources (al-Bakri, Ibn Battuta) and the name itself was used loosely for the entire Senegambian region by later medieval writers.
